_README: Single source of truth for the quiz's topic vocabulary.
Read by three things: the quiz checkboxes, the content library filter, and
the Claude classification prompt for incoming social posts.
HOW TO ADD A TOPIC
1. Copy an existing block in "topics" below and change the values.
2. Set "status" to "planned" until content exists for it (see below).
3. Put the WordPress library-topic tag slugs in "taxonomy_terms".
4. Save. Nothing else needs changing — the quiz picks it up.
FIELDS
slug            Internal id. Never change once live — analytics rows
already recorded against it would stop matching.
label           What visitors see on the quiz checkbox.
emoji           Shown before the label.
status          "live"    = offered in the quiz
"planned" = declared but hidden, for topics we intend to
cover before any content exists
taxonomy_terms  WordPress library-topic tag slugs that count as this
topic. Several may map to one topic. An empty list means
no articles can match — only social posts.
description     One sentence, written for Claude, describing what belongs
in this topic. Used when classifying social posts.
CARE POINTS
- This must stay valid JSON. No trailing commas, no // comments. If it
breaks, the quiz falls back to a built-in list and logs a warning
rather than white-screening — but the file is then being ignored.
- Display order in the quiz follows the order of this file.
- taxonomy_terms values are UNVERIFIED against the live site. They were
inferred from the prototype's old mapping, which covered only 7 of 12
topics. The five marked "needs_verification" are guesses and must be
checked against the real taxonomy once the local WordPress copy exists.
